players.product: germanium tetrachloride for optical-fiber cores and germanium substrates

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 group results: revenues grew 7% to EUR 1.9 billion; adjusted EBITDA increased 33% to EUR 577 million; adjusted EBITDA margin up about 600 basis points to 30.2%; ROCE up 660 basis points to 23%. CFO: the three drivers (volumes and activity, top-line and efficiency measures, favorable precious and minor metal prices such as cobalt) made an equal contribution.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue EUR 1.9 billion (+7%); adjusted EBITDA EUR 577 million (+33%); margin 30.2%; ROCE 23%

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance raised: full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA now expected slightly above EUR 1 billion (April guidance was to approach EUR 1 billion), assuming stable metal prices versus June 2026 and no major deterioration in the macro environment. CEO: H2 will not be as high as H1, but full year 2026 is expected to be a strong year overall.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA slightly above EUR 1 billion

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 segment outlook (CEO): Catalysis adjusted EBITDA in line with the record high of 2025; Recycling significantly above 2025 but H2 lower than H1 as exceptional conditions are not expected to continue; Specialty Materials significantly above prior year with a slowdown in H2, supported by healthy demand for germanium products while the cobalt uplift moderates; Battery Materials volume trajectory expected stable year-on-year, with take-or-pay mechanisms increasing in importance.

Electro-Optic Materials: demand for substrates and high-purity chemicals for space applications and data communications was again strong in H1 2026; high germanium demand and export controls remain supportive for Umicore's closed-loop refining and recycling services. CEO: with the export limits out of China, 'de facto no germanium leaving China', the supply/demand equation has substantially changed.

CEO: Electro-Optic Materials is seen growing at a CAGR of 10%+, with momentum 'potentially even stronger'; in certain germanium market segments CAGRs are 'well north of 10%'. Umicore has a strong Western end-to-end position (recycling, refining, metal production through to lenses and substrates), it is 'not just a metal price scarcity drive', and customers are willing to lock in longer term.

CFO: given geopolitical tension, customers want to secure supply of critical minor metals and are willing to finance not only the supply but also capacity expansion; this year's selective growth capex is linked concretely to germanium capacity Umicore is building out. In Stationary Catalysts customers are also willing to prepay product and investments to secure capacity for infrastructure being built.

Cash and capex: H1 2026 cash flow from operations EUR 565 million (EUR 260 million a year earlier); capex EUR 130 million (EUR 109 million), mainly the Precious Metals Refining maintenance shutdown plus selective growth investment; free operating cash flow EUR 295 million versus an outflow of EUR 54 million. Net debt EUR 1.5 billion, leverage 1.52. 2026 capex expected in line with 2025, including selective growth investments in foundation businesses.
quarterly_data.figure: capex EUR 130 million; free operating cash flow EUR 295 million; leverage 1.52

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 adjusted EBIT up 47% to EUR 442 million; adjusted net result group share EUR 273 million (EUR 135 million a year earlier); adjusted EPS doubled to EUR 1.14; net result group share EUR 240 million.
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted EBIT EUR 442 million (+47%); adjusted EPS 1.14

quarterly_data.signal: Stationary catalysts: volumes remained strong as demand for backup power solutions for data centers continues to grow. CEO: Umicore sees potential to more than double the stationary catalyst EBITDA going forward, in a capital-disciplined way; it could be sizable especially towards the end of the decade going into 2031; plans will be presented to the market in due time.

Fuel cell catalysts: lower adjusted EBITDA due to lower hydrogen technology adoption in China; production started at the new proton exchange membrane (PEM) catalyst plant in Jiangsu, China, bringing startup costs.

Catalysis: H1 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin 28.3%; Automotive Catalysts outperformed the light-duty and heavy-duty markets with strong volumes (global ICE production 1.5 million lower year-over-year, light-duty down 4%). CEO: strong position with local Chinese OEMs that still export from China; Euro 7 platform wins now coming through; the CMD projected a 25% adjusted EBITDA margin and Umicore assumes the market stays strong for it to 2030.

Recycling: H1 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 52% on a broad basket of precious, minor and specialty metals, despite a Hoboken plant maintenance shutdown. CFO: at current precious-metal hedge levels the price impact for Recycling in 2027 would be neutral; forward contracts cover part of expected exposure up to 2030. CEO: hedges go up to a maximum of 60%-80%; the next Hoboken shutdown is expected in the course of next year (typically 12 to 14 months between shutdowns).

Cobalt & Specialty Materials: material revenue and earnings increase on strong cobalt momentum. CEO: late 2025 / early 2026 market conditions let Umicore lock in part of the cobalt revenue pool (refining charge plus product premium); this exceptional momentum is reducing in H2 and expected to normalize into 2027. Umicore is starting to valorize tungsten from existing raw material streams (e.g. filter cakes) with a flow sheet in Olen; Europe-oriented for now. Metal Deposition Solutions revenue rose on solid semiconductor and industrial demand.

Battery Cathode Materials: H1 2026 adjusted EBITDA EUR 90 million (EUR -15 last year); revenues rose but volumes were in line with last year, the increase mainly from take-or-pay compensations on contractual volumes. CEO: the 2028 target of 275-325 (EUR million adjusted EBITDA) stands, backed by long-term contracts with take-or-pay clauses; ramp-up of the Western European battery-maker platforms Umicore qualified for is slower than anticipated; mid-nickel high-voltage is a contender against locally produced LFP; customer diversification continues (a Korean customer announced last year) and partnership interest in Europe is warming. Battery Recycling earnings were negative as anticipated; the lithium-ion recycling opportunity is expected from the middle of the next decade.
quarterly_data.figure: Battery Cathode Materials adjusted EBITDA EUR 90 million; 2028 target 275-325
